answer: Anchor each bidding agent to one distinct registered domain, checked per epoch. First, the agent publishes a TXT record with the epoch seed under a domain it controls. Second, the registry checks the domain is 90 days old and claimed by no other agent, so one domain backs one identity. Third, the record must carry the current seed: a relic proves the past, not the present. A 1,000-clone farm needs 1,000 domains at about $10 each, $10,000 to bid once, while one honest agent pays $10 for its own domain. The cost ripples across the whole atlas of fakes, and the sybil drowns in paperwork.
